fields.description:
## Context / Problem

S1–S4 change a rule that authors and agents are told about in prose: "record file_impact or
your attestation invalidates on any commit". Once an explicit no-file-impact declaration exists, the
prose is incomplete in the way that matters most — an author reading today's guidance has no
way to learn that the third option exists, and the coaching that fires on an undeclared leaf
would keep pointing at the only remedy it knows.

This story closes the documentation gap. It changes prose only — but prose lives in FILES, so
this ticket declares those files as ordinary `file_impact` paths. It is NOT a `none` ticket:
`none` means the work touches no repo file at all, and this one edits four.

## Approach

Update the four author-facing surfaces that describe file impact, each in one place:

- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the tri-state, what each state does to attestation freshness,
  the container roll-up rule (a `none` child is neutral; an UNDECLARED child still poisons),
  and the fact that flipping the declaration invalidates the attestation via the material
  fingerprint.
- `docs/ticket-model.md` — the tri-state as part of the ticket model, next to file impact.
- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` — the author's on-ramp (`rebar explain plan`):
  when to declare `none` and when NOT to, and that the claim is reviewed by the
  `no-file-impact` criterion, so the reason must be substantive.
- `docs/event-schema.md` — final wording for the FILE_IMPACT event's new keys, reconciled with
  whatever S1 landed.

The criteria guide is NOT hand-edited here — S4 regenerates it. This story only cross-links to
it.

## Scope

- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/ticket-model.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`,
  `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`.
- No source-behavior change: the one file under `src/` is a packaged prose guide, and the
  ticket touches no logic, no schema, and no test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents all three code-impact states and their effect on
      attestation freshness, including that an UNDECLARED empty impact still falls back to
      whole-HEAD (checked: the section exists and names all three states).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the container rule that a `none` child is neutral
      while an undeclared child poisons inheritance (checked: same section).
- [ ] `rebar explain plan` output tells an author when to declare `none`, when not to, and
      that the claim is LLM-reviewed (checked: `rebar explain plan | grep`-able assertions in
      the existing guide test).
- [ ] No file under `src/rebar` other than `_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` is modified
      (checked: the change's own diff, asserted at review time).
- [ ] The docs state explicitly that `none` means NO repo file is touched — a docs-only or
      test-only ticket declares paths, not `none` (checked: the gate-doc section says so).
- [ ] `make lint` passes and the full test suite is unchanged and green.
fields.title: Document the tri-state file-impact scope in the gate, ticket-model, event-schema and author guide
